investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was written, causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents Swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out before reaching a running/idle/ready state. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is currently scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary: The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have their allocatable VM slots fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Preemption is also blocked because no lower-priority victims exist.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector (likely a label or taint requiring kata/peerpods runtime class), so they are structurally ineligible regardless of capacity.

Tertiary: A cluster scaling event (node drain, node failure, or autoscaler delay) may have temporarily reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously sufficient count to 2, exhausting capacity.

Lower probability: A quota or LimitRange change on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource could have reduced the per-namespace or per-node ceiling without removing nodes, producing the same Insufficient signal.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T23:35–23:40Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster has 0/6 nodes available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) and that agent pod could not be scheduled, the probe never reached the state-polling step, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unwritten and the contract fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: 2 nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). This prevented the eval runner from creating the prerequisite remote agent VM, so the probe timed out after ~146 s without producing any evidence, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required fields missing. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no capacity remains for a new remote-agent pod, and preemption found no evictable victims. This directly matches the scheduler message in failed-check.message and sibling.remote-agent-create and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

[Possible] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, any single additional VM request will fail. A recent node label change or pod spec affinity change could have shrunk the eligible pool.

[Possible] Cluster under-provisioning for peak load — the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have insufficient total VM slots for concurrent eval runs plus production workloads, causing transient exhaustion during the eval window.

[Lower confidence] A change in the remote-agent pod spec (resource requests, tolerations, or affinity rules) could have made the pod unschedulable on nodes that previously accepted it. No suspect changes in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges support this hypothesis; it remains speculative.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was written, causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents Swarm runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out before reaching a running/idle/ready state. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval configuration or code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is currently scoped to this observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary: The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have their allocatable VM slots fully consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Preemption is also blocked because no lower-priority victims exist.

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector (likely a label or taint requiring kata/peerpods runtime class), so they are structurally ineligible regardless of capacity.

Tertiary: A cluster scaling event (node drain, node failure, or autoscaler delay) may have temporarily reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously sufficient count to 2, exhausting capacity.

Lower probability: A quota or LimitRange change on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource could have reduced the per-namespace or per-node ceiling without removing nodes, producing the same Insufficient signal.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T23:35–23:40Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster has 0/6 nodes available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) and that agent pod could not be scheduled, the probe never reached the state-polling step, leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unwritten and the contract fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: 2 nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). This prevented the eval runner from creating the prerequisite remote agent VM, so the probe timed out after ~146 s without producing any evidence, causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with all four required fields missing. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-06T23:35–23:40Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real Kubernetes scheduling constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. When the eval runner called createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), the scheduler could not place the pod on any of the 6 available nodes — 2 due to Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch — and preemption was not possible. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~142–146 seconds until the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a complete contract gap across all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which is the call that triggers remote pod scheduling

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract at lines 266-269 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these could be satisfied without a running pod
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for the eval's new pod. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If this selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, the effective capacity would drop. No suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges supports this as a recent code change, but it remains a plausible infrastructure-side cause.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: only 2 nodes are configured with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource, which may be insufficient to absorb concurrent eval runs plus production workloads. This would cause intermittent scheduling failures under load.

UNLIKELY — eval runner misconfiguration causing incorrect node selector on the pod spec: would require a code change in run-status-probes.mjs or the agent creation path, but sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty and the sibling checks show the same message, making a runner-side regression less likely than an infrastructure capacity issue.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization on the 2 eligible nodes in the production cluster. If slots are fully consumed, identify and terminate any stale or leaked remote agent pods to free capacity.

Determine whether the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector are intentionally excluded (e.g., wrong machine type for kata peer-pods) or whether a label drift or misconfiguration has reduced the schedulable pool below its intended size.
If capacity is confirmed exhausted, evaluate whether additional nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource need to be provisioned or whether the VM slot limit per node can be increased.

Review the eval runner's cleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (withCleanup at line 1916) to confirm that eval-created remote agent pods are reliably terminated after each run and are not accumulating as leaked pods that consume VM slots.

Monitor the next scheduled eval run after any remediation to confirm remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all return to passing status and produce the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message).

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (not exhausted) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run — this would rule out capacity exhaustion and point to a different scheduling constraint.
A successful re-run of the remote-agent-runtime eval immediately after the failure window, with no cluster changes, would suggest a transient scheduling blip rather than sustained exhaustion.
Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed in a way that incorrectly excludes the 2 kata-capable nodes — this would shift the root cause from capacity to misconfiguration.

A passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime at any point during the same eval window — none are present, but such a result would weaken the exhaustion hypothesis.

Scheduler logs showing the pod was rejected for a reason other than Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm (e.g., resource quota, taint/toleration mismatch) would indicate a different infrastructure constraint.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting remote agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity message rather than waiting for a scheduling timeout.
Add a remote-agent-pod-cleanup eval that verifies no orphaned remote agent pods remain in the cluster after each eval cycle, catching leaked pods before they exhaust VM slot capacity.

Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is at or above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting on pool shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Consider adding a warning-level check that fires when kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing earlier signal before full exhaustion causes eval failures.
